These islands are of great interest since they create narrow gorges through which the water can reach greater speeds. However, soundings in this area are more irregular and can be more challenging to moor the MTV. Average current speeds for Point Wilson are around 1.5 m/s, while maximum speeds are around 2.3 m/s. For the San Juan Islands, average speeds are around 1.5 m/s, but maximum speeds are around 3.2 m/s, with current speeds reaching 4.4 m/s at some particular locations and times. These locations are quite protected from waves due to their geographical locations, and the maximum significant wave height in the middle of Admiralty Inlet, where NOAA’s NDBC buoy 46088 is located, only reaches 1.7 m. Wind speeds at this location average 3 m/s, while the maximum recorded wind speed for 2021 was 19.5 m/s. Western Passage The Western Passage has one of the world’s most extreme tidal ranges. Therefore, using jack-ups is not an option for this location, and an internal or external mooring system will be needed. Available support and at-sea infrastructure around the area are scarce, and deployment of the MTV could be a challenge. However, steady current speeds average at 1.5 m/s and reach maximums of 3.2 m/s at some locations. Wave data for this location was not readily available, and figures of significant wave heights at more exposed locations were obtained, assuming waves would be attenuated when reaching Western Passage. The maximum significant wave height for a 5-year return period is 4 m. The average recorded speed for wind speeds was 3.8 m/s, while the maximum recorded speed for 2021 was 19.6 m/s. Final Technical Report 17/57 Piscataqua River Piscataqua River presents great soundings for jack-up leg use while allowing for the use of the internal mooring system as well. The proposed areas for this location are between General Sullivan Bridge and Frankfort Island, with current speeds averaging 2 m/s and maximum speeds reaching 2.9 m/s. For this location, there is no available data for waves or wind. However, due to its geographical location, thresholds imposed by the analysis of the rest of the locations are estimated to cover potential environmental conditions given at this location. 3.2.3 River location – Mississippi River Riverine energy technologies extract the kinetic energy from flowing river water to generate electricity. Although not technically a marine resource, as part of the natural hydrological cycle, precipitation from drainage basins, groundwater springs, and snow melt feed rivers that flow toward lakes, seas, and oceans. Current speeds in the rivers were lower and oscillated around 0.7 m/s and 1.37 m/s. The proposed river location for evaluation was on the Mississippi River, downstream of St. Louis, MO. Bathymetry at this location makes it suitable for the use of the jack-up legs or the internal mooring system after carrying out the corresponding detailed bathymetry analysis.
